newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine, Russia strike up post-Soviet friendship.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine, Russia strike up post-Soviet friendship.

text.p: Russia and Ukraine officially made friends on Saturday, signing a friendship treaty after years of acrimony over the Black Sea Fleet, post-Soviet debts and trade restrictions.
"This declaration puts an end to the so-called Sevastopol problem," President Leonid Kuchma said after signing the treaty with Russian President Boris Yeltsin.
"We have no problems left. There are none. I am taking with me the good mood and the smiles of the Ukrainian people, the people of Kiev," Yeltsin said.

Five summits have failed to find a long-term settlement sharing out the fleet based at the port of Sevastopol on the Crimean peninsula which Nikita Khrushchev transferred from Russia to Soviet Ukraine in a largely symbolic gesture in 1954.
Russian parliamentarians have urged the Kremlin to claim Sevastopol, saying it was excluded from the original deal.
Russia and Ukraine also finalised a deal ending differences over Kiev's massive energy debt to Moscow.

Called the "zero option", it involves Kiev leasing bays and land at Sevastopol for Russia to base its fleet and Russia compensating Ukraine for nuclear missiles removed from its territory in return for cancelling Ukraine's state energy debt.

Ukraine, seeking to free itself from centuries of Moscow domination, has turned to the West and is seeking strategic partnerships elsewhere -- but both countries feel they still need strong relations with each other.
"Europe wants to accept those who can live in peace and cooperation into its community. Ukrainian-Russian relations in the near future will be a model of bilateral relations.
"Today Boris Nikolayevich (Yeltsin) and I made serious progress towards this end," Kuchma said.

Yeltsin was in determined and upbeat mood after he signed four documents including the treaty, a political declaration on bilateral and international issues and statements on the Black Sea Fleet and on economic and space cooperation.
"We should force this treaty to work," he said, jabbing his finger in the air.

He urged the two countries' parliaments to ratify the friendship treaty, adding: "It was signed not by the presidents' will but first and foremost by the peoples' will. The Russians and the Ukrainians gave us an order to stand up to the task." Yeltsin earlier laid a wreath at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier and said his ministers must do as they were told.
"I will tell ministers in Moscow: 'Just try forgetting that Ukraine is the priority of all priorities and you'll have the president to deal with," he declared.
Yeltsin also referred to the fact that Ukrainian producers have to pay value added tax twice -- once at home and once in Russia.
"Today we tax Ukraine twice for its goods. This is real banditism. I wasn't informed about that. If I had known I would have taken off someone's head long ago," Yeltsin said.
He said he wanted Russians to think of their neighbours. "We should shape the psychology of the people so they wake in the morning and ask 'What have you done for Ukraine?'".

The ground for Yeltsin's first state visit to Ukraine was prepared by his Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, who in lengthy talks with Kuchma on Wednesday agreed Russia would lease Sevastopol for 20 years for its part of the disputed fleet.
Kuchma and Chernomyrdin said they had solved most other problems and that the road to the summit meeting was open.
